blog.title: Engineering Blog | officeParser
blog.author: Harsh Ankur
blog.description: How document formats work inside, how officeParser reads and writes them, where it falls short, and how to chunk documents for retrieval. Written by Harsh Ankur, author of officeParser.

posts.title: What is Actually Inside a .docx File? An Architectural Deep Dive
posts.description: A tour of the .docx package: parts and relationships, runs that Word splits mid-word, lists stored in another file, merged cells, text boxes, and field codes, and what officeParser makes of them.
posts.deck: Most developers assume a Word document is styled text in a zip archive. It is closer to a small database: parts tied together by relationships, text split into runs, lists defined in another file, and text boxes nested inside drawings.

posts.title: How PowerPoint Really Stores a Slide: Coordinate Systems, Master Trees, and DrawingML
posts.description: Why a slide is a canvas and not a text flow: English Metric Units, the theme, master and layout chain, the shape tree, speaker notes, and why reading order is hard.
posts.deck: A word processing file flows from top to bottom. A presentation is the opposite: a set of separate canvases where shapes sit at coordinates, formatting is inherited through four layers, and every length is a whole number of units, 914,400 to the inch.

posts.title: Why PDF Text Extraction is Unforgivingly Hard
posts.description: A PDF has no words, paragraphs, or reading order. Positioned glyphs, missing spaces, font encodings, ligatures, multi-column pages, and the XY-cut that rebuilds reading order.
posts.deck: PDF describes how a page looks, not what it says. It knows how to paint glyphs at coordinates. Getting text back out means reconstructing what a reader's eye does without being told.

posts.title: Security War Stories: Decompression Bombs, SSRF, and Hardening an Office Parser
posts.description: Four holes found and fixed in officeParser: a ZIP header that lies about its size, SSRF through PDF rendering, spreadsheet repeat attributes, and nesting that runs the stack out.
posts.deck: A parser's whole job is to open files that someone else built. Here are four ways a crafted document attacked officeParser, and what the code does about each one now.

posts.title: From String Scraping to AST: The Architectural Evolution of officeParser
posts.description: Why returning one flat string hit a ceiling, and how a typed AST made conversion between Office, Markdown, HTML, and LaTeX possible.
posts.deck: For more than six years officeParser returned a string. Here is why that stopped being enough, what replaced it, and the rule that has governed every feature since.

posts.title: Where officeParser is the Wrong Tool: An Honest Engineering Guide
posts.shortTitle: Where officeParser is the Wrong Tool
posts.description: The jobs officeParser does not do: PDFs that match Word exactly, formula recalculation, legacy .doc files, writing spreadsheets and slides, macros, and TeX typesetting, and what to use instead.
posts.deck: Most documentation reads like a sales pitch, with the drawbacks in the fine print. I would rather be plain: here are the problems officeParser does not solve, and the tools to use instead.

posts.title: Document Chunking for Retrieval Done Right: Beyond Naive Token Windows
posts.description: Why a sliding token window shreds tables and orphans headings, what chunking on document structure fixes, and what officeParser's chunker does and does not do.
posts.deck: Teams tune embedding models and re-rankers while feeding them chunks that were cut in the wrong places. Here is what a fixed-size splitter does to a real document, and what chunking on the document's structure fixes.
